question: On a multi-lane roadway posted at 35 mph, may the single-lane regulatory-sign size be used, and what size must a STOP sign still use?
model_answer: Direct Answer: No. On a multi-lane roadway posted at 35 mph, the reduced (Minimum-column / single-lane-appropriate) sizes may not be used, because the MUTCD restricts those smaller sizes to low-speed facilities with operating speeds of 30 mph or less; the full Conventional Road sizes are required as the floor. However, the evidence provided does not include the regulatory sign size table that specifies the exact numeric dimension for the STOP sign (R1-1) on multi-lane conventional roads, so the specific STOP sign size cannot be stated from this evidence. Standards (mandatory): - "The sign dimensions prescribed in the sign size tables in the various Parts and Chapters in this Manual and in the 'Standard Highway Signs' publication (see Section 1A.05) shall be used unless engineering judgment determines that other sizes are appropriate in accordance with the following. Except as provided in Paragraph 3 of this Section, where engineering judgment determines that sizes smaller than the prescribed dimensions are appropriate for use, the sign dimensions shall not be less than the minimum dimensions specified in this Manual. The sizes shown in the Minimum columns that are smaller than the sizes shown in the Conventional Road columns in the various sign size tables in this Manual shall only be used on low-speed roadways, alleys, site roadways open to public travel, and on low-volume rural roads with operating speeds of 30 mph or less; and only where the reduced legend size would be adequate for the regulation or warning or where physical conditions preclude the use of larger sizes." — A 35-mph multi-lane roadway exceeds the 30-mph operating-speed threshold, so the smaller Minimum-column sizes are not permitted there. Guidance (recommended): - For guide sign legends, Table 2D-2 provides separate Single-Lane and Multi-Lane columns by speed range (Less than 30 mph, 30–40 mph, Greater than 40 mph); a 35-mph multi-lane roadway falls in the Multi-Lane 30–40 mph column, not the Single-Lane column. - For school-area regulatory signs, "The sizes in the Oversized column should be used on roadways that have four or more lanes with posted speed limits of 40 mph or higher" — a 35-mph multi-lane road does not trigger the Oversized recommendation, but the Conventional Road sizes still apply as the minimum. Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Table 2D-2 (Sheet 1, Post-Mounted Signs) shows distinct Multi-Lane columns for the 30–40 mph range, confirming that multi-lane roads at 35 mph use larger legend sizes than the single-lane columns. - [Image 2] Table 7B-1 lists Conventional Road, Minimum, and Oversized sizes for school-area signs, and its notes state that minimum sign sizes for multi-lane conventional roads shall be as shown in the Conventional Road column. - [Image 5] Page 94 shows the Section 2A.07 Standard text restricting Minimum-column sizes to low-speed roadways with operating speeds of 30 mph or less. Citations: - Section 2A.07 Standard §2 (p.45) - Section 2D.07 Guidance §5 (p.210) - Section 7B.01 Guidance §3 (p.972) - Table 2D-2 (p.210) - Table 7B-1 (p.971) - Page 94 Note on insufficiency: The specific STOP sign (R1-1) size table for conventional roads is not included in the provided evidence, so the exact required STOP sign dimension (e.g., a specific width × height) cannot be quoted here. What can be established is that at 35 mph on a multi-lane road, no size smaller than the Conventional Road column value may be used.
gold_answer: For regulatory signs other than STOP, the single-lane size may be used at 35 mph or less. The STOP-sign exception remains: the multi-lane STOP size is 36 x 36 inches.
